newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INSTANT VIEW - NZ easing seen after Mar qtr CPI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - NZ easing seen after Mar qtr CPI.

text.p: Following is a list of analysts' reactions to New Zealand March quarter inflation data published at 2245 GMT on Tuesday.
"It reinforces what the Reserve Bank was saying a month ago that we can have easier monetary conditions. I suspect they will come out and say that conditions are too tight," he said.

"I think you will see conditions, at the end of the day, easier than they are right now. It just says, together with what we are picking up from the rest of the economy, that the economy is pretty slow at the moment. The inflation rate is coming down quicker than had been expected, so the response to that should be easier monetary conditions."
Countering that, Byett said, was the prospect of good growth over 1998 and 1999, with associated inflationary pressures.
"Inflationary pressures are going to creep up by then and 1998 is starting to come into the Reserve Bank's horizon," he said.
BANKERS TRUST NZ CHIEF ECONOMIST DAVID PLANK

"I think they (the Reserve Bank) would expect the market to ease conditions, which it is doing, but I don't think there is any reason necessarily for the Reserve Bank to come out and say anything. The numbers are consistent with its view.
"They already have a very optimistic view of inflation going forward so I don't think they will say conditions will ease necessarily any more than they wanted back in March," he said.
While conditions eased considerably since the release of the data at 2245 GMT, they are still tighter than the Reserve Bank had assumed in March.

"So they've still got quite a way to go before you even get back to where they were in March. I would not have thought they would want conditions to ease necessarily any more than that, and the market may do it for them," he said.
